question: Can a lifted shortest-path algorithm independently recover first nontrivial holonomy, and when do girth and the first faithful moment alone lose information?
scope: All connected labeled simple graphs on 2–4 vertices, plus four fixed cactus graphs. All Z4 spanning-tree gauge assignments.
primary: Lifted BFS, walk moments and simple-cycle DFS agree on shortest nontrivial loop; moment inversion recovers all four closed-walk flux counts at every computed length.
success: Zero primary mismatches; report all control misses and collision witnesses, including no collision where applicable.
limitations: Fixed protocol committed before evaluation; not externally preregistered or blinded. Cactus families deliberately selected following study 020. No novelty or speed superiority claim.
